chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Jibla narrated from al-Hakam ibn Aymen, from Muhammad ibn Tamam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah

"Someone sends you his regards and says to you: Guarantee me intercession." He said: "Is he from our followers?" I said: "Yes." He said: "His matter is more important than that." I said: "He is a man who follows Ali but does not know the successors after him." He said: "He is astray." I said: "He acknowledged all the Imams but denied the last one." He said: "He is like one who acknowledged Jesus and denied Muhammad, or acknowledged Muhammad and denied Jesus. We seek refuge in Allah from denying any of His proof.".
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of believing in Ali but denying the subsequent Imams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) distinguishes between mere political allegiance to Ali and the theological necessity of recognizing the continuous line of Imams, declaring that partial belief is insufficient. He employs a profound analogy, comparing the denial of a subsequent Imam to denying Prophet Muhammad while accepting Jesus, thereby elevating the status of the Imams as God's definitive proofs (Hujaj). This highlights the Shia doctrine that faith is incomplete without explicit acceptance of the divinely appointed successors.
